title: Trust in the CDC and FDA hits record lows, Gallup finds — just 26% and 25% rate them good or excellent
excerpt: Only 26% of Americans rate the CDC's job excellent or good and 25% say the same of the FDA — the lowest marks either agency has ever received in Gallup's surveys.
content:
Public confidence in the nation's two leading health agencies has fallen to the lowest levels Gallup has ever recorded, with just 26 percent of Americans rating the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention as doing an "excellent" or "good" job and 25 percent saying the same of the Food and Drug Administration.

The survey, which reached 1,000 people during the first half of September, found the CDC down five percentage points from 2025, about 14 points below its ratings through the COVID-19 pandemic, and far below its high of 66 percent back in 2017. The FDA scored a point lower, down from 27 percent in 2025 and well below its 2017 high of 46 percent.

The two health agencies graded lower than the 10 other federal agencies included in the poll, which was topped by the Postal Service at 58 percent. They were also the only two agencies that received more "poor" ratings than excellent-or-good ratings — the worst showing for each in Gallup's historical surveys, which began in 2003 for the CDC and 2009 for the FDA.

Gallup pointed to a difficult year of headlines: measles and cyclospora outbreaks, and sweeping upheaval inside the Department of Health and Human Services under Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., including substantial leadership turnover, slashed workforces, and regulatory policies criticized by industry groups and public health experts, such as attempted changes to the childhood vaccine schedule.

The numbers also reveal a sharp partisan split that has flipped with the administration in power. Among Republicans, positive ratings of the CDC rose from 19 percent in 2024 to 32 percent in 2026, and of the FDA from 23 percent to 36 percent. Among Democrats, the CDC fell from 65 percent favorable in 2024 to 20 percent in 2026, and the FDA from 47 percent to 18 percent.

Congress will weigh in again in the coming months on funding for the agencies, after lawmakers pushed back on White House proposals to substantially cut budgets and reorganize their structure — though news reports suggest parts of the agencies have not received their anticipated levels of funding.

The timing matters for Webb County readers: Gallup notes health care, above all its cost, is a top issue for voters heading into the November 3 midterms. When the agencies that police food safety and track outbreaks lose public trust, the practical question is not just political — it is whether residents believe the warnings those agencies issue when the next outbreak or recall arrives.

Sources:

  • Fierce Healthcare, "Few Americans say CDC, FDA are doing a good job: survey," Oct. 22, 2026 (reporting Gallup survey)
